## Segment summary
A young man in a workshop demonstrates how to build a simple, cube-shaped robot called a "desk-buddy" using three components: an IMU, an OLED screen, and a microcontroller. He explains that the project costs less than $5 and requires only four wires per component to connect them via the I2C communication protocol. The video uses text overlays and inset images to illustrate the components and wiring process.

speech.text: Here's how to build this desk buddy for less than five bucks and all it takes is three components.
An IMU, an OLED screen and a microcontroller. To make this little robot is super simple,
as both the IMU and the OLED talk over I squared C. So what that means is that they
share the same two data lines. All you need to do is connect power and ground,
then SDA and SCL, four wires per component and you're done.
